rules: This is a detective game played entirely inside this PDF. Click the blue buttons to make your choices and move between pages.
Your inventory is shown at the top of every page. Some choices are greyed out until you are carrying the right item.
Page numbers are shuffled, so flipping ahead will not help you. Use the buttons, not the scroll bar.
There are {endings} different endings. Some are triumphant. Some are educational.

start.title: Start
start.text: It is 3 a.m. Your phone buzzes on the nightstand: an alert from your homelab. Something is very wrong.

ddos.title: Homelab DDoS
ddos.text: Traffic graphs are through the roof. Thousands of requests per second are hammering your homelab. The router fans are screaming. You have to act now.

choices.label: Close all open ports on the router

read_logs.title: Read the traffic logs
read_logs.text: Every single request carries the same User-Agent: 'GregBot/1.0'. Greg is your friend. Greg is a sysadmin. Greg has a sense of humor. Or does he?

choices.label: Close all open ports on the router

block_ua.title: Block the User-Agent
block_ua.text: One line in the reverse proxy config. The traffic drops for exactly three seconds, then returns with a new User-Agent: 'GregBot/1.1'. Someone is mocking you.

choices.label: Check who is connected to the router
Close all open ports on the router

call_greg.title: Call Greg
call_greg.text: Greg picks up on the ninth ring. 'It is 3 a.m. This better be a death.' You explain. He yawns. 'Turn it off and on again. I am going back to sleep.'

choices.label: Follow his advice: pull the plug
Hang up and close the ports

greg_logs.title: Greg wakes up
greg_logs.text: Silence. Then: 'That is NOT my bot. Check your IoT junk, this looks like a Mirai variant.' He sounds fully awake now, and slightly offended.

choices.label: Check who is connected to the router
Ask why he knows so much about this
Close all open ports on the router

accuse_greg.title: Accuse Greg
accuse_greg.text: 'You think I would DDoS my own friend?!' Greg hangs up. Your phone shows one missed call from him and zero chances of more help tonight. You feel a little bad.

choices.label: Check who is connected to the router
Close all open ports on the router

check_dhcp.title: The DHCP list
check_dhcp.text: Fourteen devices: laptop, phone, TV, the cat feeder, the smart fridge, and one host called 'unknown-7f3a' that you have never seen in your life.

choices.label: Close all open ports on the router

fridge.title: Unplug the fridge
fridge.text: The fridge was running firmware from 2014 and was indeed part of a botnet, but a very small part. The attack does not even notice. Your ice cream begins to melt for nothing.

choices.label: Close all open ports on the router

block_host.title: Block unknown-7f3a
block_host.text: Blocked. A second later 'unknown-7f3b' appears. Then 7f3c. New hosts keep spawning, and they are not coming from the Internet. They are coming from inside your server.

choices.label: Close all open ports on the router

cat_cam.title: Server room camera
cat_cam.text: On the feed: Pixel the cat, asleep on top of the server, one paw on the keyboard. Suspicious, but she has been there since 2 a.m. and has an alibi: she is a cat.

choices.label: Close all open ports on the router

remove_internet.title: Remove Internet connection
remove_internet.text: You rip the ethernet cable out of the router. The blinking lights go quiet. But the attack was already writing to your disks when the link dropped.

close_ports.title: Close all open ports on router
close_ports.text: You log into the router and shut every forwarded port: SSH, HTTPS, the Jellyfin stream, everything. The router is quiet for a moment, then the logs start scrolling again.

data_loss_a.title: 20% data loss
data_loss_a.text: A fifth of your files are gone or corrupted. The rest of the lab is cut off from the world.

choices.label: Plug the ethernet cable back in

data_loss_b.title: 20% data loss
data_loss_b.text: The ports are closed, but the attacker was already inside. A fifth of your files are gone or corrupted, and the system is acting strangely.

choices.label: Look at the system more closely

no_internet.title: No internet
no_internet.text: Silence. Without a connection you cannot look up fixes, ask for help or download anything. You are alone with the damage.

choices.label: Plug the ethernet cable back in
Search your desk for anything useful
Knock on Mrs. Nagy's door for Wi-Fi
Wait for the sun to come up

desk_search.title: Search the desk
desk_search.text: Under three tangled chargers you find a USB stick labelled 'RESCUE - tested never'. Past you was either a genius or an optimist. Behind it, a sticky note: 'check the attic'.

choices.label: Go back to the server room

attic.title: The attic
attic.text: Dust, a plastic Christmas tree and a shoebox. Inside: a laminated card in your handwriting. 'OFFSITE BACKUP KEY - bucket homelab-bkp'. You had completely forgotten that you made one.

choices.label: Go back to the server room

neighbor_wifi.title: Mrs. Nagy's Wi-Fi
neighbor_wifi.text: Mrs. Nagy opens the door in a dressing gown, holding a rolling pin. After a lecture about what time it is, she gives you the password: 'macska1234'. Her router is, somehow, very secure.

choices.label: Download a rescue ISO and flash a USB stick

flash_usb.title: Flash a rescue USB
flash_usb.text: At her kitchen table you download the ISO and flash it while Mrs. Nagy watches you like a hawk. Twenty minutes and one cookie later, you hold a bootable stick.

choices.label: Go home and check the server

logic_bomb.title: 3:33 a.m.
logic_bomb.text: A cron job nobody wrote wakes up. Every fan on the rack changes pitch, the console fills with red text, and /boot disappears. The DDoS was only a smokescreen: the real attack was already inside.

firewall_logs.title: Firewall logs
firewall_logs.text: Between thousands of junk requests hides a single successful SSH login at 02:41, using a key you did not create.

authkeys.title: authorized_keys
authkeys.text: Three keys. Yours. 'greg@old-laptop' from 2021. And one with the comment 'backup@localhost', added at 02:41 tonight.

choices.label: Call Greg about his old key

remove_key.title: Remove the key
remove_key.text: You delete the key. The terminal answers: 'Connection closed by remote host.' He was already using something else, something much deeper than SSH.

plug_back.title: Plug back ethernet
plug_back.text: The link light turns green again. For a few seconds everything looks fine. Then the traffic graph spikes.

still_attacking.title: Still attacking
still_attacking.text: The attack never stopped. Whoever is behind it is still hammering your lab, and the router is wide open again.

choices.label: Close all open ports on the router

kernel_deleted.title: Kernel deleted
kernel_deleted.text: You open the console. The kernel has been deleted. The machine is still running from memory, but it will not survive a reboot. You need to get it back, and fast.

choices.label: Ask an AI how to recover the kernel
Ask Reddit how to recover the kernel
Search the Arch wiki on your phone

greg_kernel.title: Greg, again
greg_kernel.text: Greg answers on the first ring. Grumpy, but he cannot resist a broken kernel. 'Do NOT paste random commands. Boot a live USB, chroot in, reinstall from the package cache. Like a civilized person.'

choices.label: Admit you have no USB stick

no_usb.title: No USB stick
no_usb.text: 'Then make one,' says Greg. 'You need a laptop, an ISO and a connection. Phone hotspot will do.' He hangs up to go back to bed. Again.

choices.label: Tether your phone and flash a stick

flash_usb_home.title: Flash a rescue USB
flash_usb_home.text: The phone hotspot crawls, the ISO downloads, the progress bar lies about its percentage. Eventually you hold a bootable stick with a freshly written 'RESCUE' label.

arch_wiki.title: The Arch wiki
arch_wiki.text: Three hours of reading compressed into twelve minutes. Verdict: you need a live USB, a chroot and patience. It also says, in bold, not to run commands you do not understand.

choices.label: Ignore the bold text, ask an AI

ask_ai.title: Ask an AI
ask_ai.text: You paste the panic-induced error logs into an AI chatbot. It confidently outputs a multi-step kernel compilation and reinstallation command string. You copy-paste and execute it.

ask_reddit.title: Ask Reddit
ask_reddit.text: You post on r/homelab with the title: 'PLEASE HELP MY KERNEL IS DELETED'. Almost instantly a user called kev_the_kernel replies with a helpful-looking shell script.

reddit_comments.title: The other comments
reddit_comments.text: The top comment, from a moderator: 'Boot a live USB. Never paste scripts from strangers.' Kev's reply was posted forty seconds after you. Nobody diagnoses a kernel in forty seconds. Unless they already knew.

unknown_event.title: Something happened
unknown_event.text: The terminal flashes a cascade of cryptic messages. The screen freezes for a moment. You aren't entirely sure what just executed, but the system state has fundamentally shifted.

choices.label: Try to revert using the AI method
Inspect what the AI command changed

check_changes.title: Inspect the damage
check_changes.text: The AI built a kernel for the wrong CPU architecture, set the root password to 'password' 'for convenience' and disabled the firewall 'to avoid conflicts'. Impressive, honestly.

choices.label: Reboot and hope for the best
Ask the AI to fix its own mistake

panic_loop.title: Kernel panic
panic_loop.text: The machine boots, panics, reboots, panics. A loop. The fans spin up and down like a broken ventilator. Each cycle takes forty seconds, and your patience takes forty seconds less.

ai_followup.title: The AI apologizes
ai_followup.text: 'You are absolutely right, and I apologize!' it says, then offers a cleaner solution: 'rm -rf /boot /etc /var' followed by a fresh install. It sounds extremely confident.

ai_wipe.title: Run the command
ai_wipe.text: The terminal scrolls for a very long time. Then it stops. Then the terminal itself disappears, because the thing that was running it no longer exists.

blackout.title: Everything goes black
blackout.text: The monitors click off. The server chassis fans wind down to complete silence. Total darkness fills the room.

choices.label: Hit the physical power button to restart

phone_dm.title: A new message
phone_dm.text: One new DM from kev_the_kernel: 'thx for the root password lol. have fun rebuilding'. He deletes the message while you are still reading it.

choices.label: Hit the physical power button to restart

restart.title: Restart
restart.text: The BIOS splash screen appears. Services begin initializing one by one as the OS boots back up from disk.

rescue_usb.title: The rescue USB
rescue_usb.text: The stick boots on the first try, which feels like a personal gift from past you. A live shell, a blinking cursor, and your dead disks waiting to be mounted.

choices.label: Mount, chroot and reinstall the kernel

kernel_ok.title: Kernel reinstalled
kernel_ok.text: The package cache comes through. A fresh kernel sits in /boot again. Before rebooting, you notice the disk still has other surprises hiding in it.

choices.label: Scan the disk for hidden tools

reboot_risky.title: Reboot right now
reboot_risky.text: The system boots. Twenty minutes later the logic bomb you did not remove fires a second time and the kernel vanishes again. At least the rescue stick is still warm.

scan_backdoor.title: Hidden tools
scan_backdoor.text: Hidden in /etc and /usr/lib: a logic-bomb cron job, a rogue SSH key and a text file called README_KEV.txt: 'gg ez - kev_the_kernel'. Whoever he is, he is proud of it.

choices.label: Document it, delete it and reboot

clean_boot.title: A clean boot
clean_boot.text: The BIOS splash, then the login prompt. No red text, no strange kernel modules. Services start one by one, politely, like a system with nothing to hide.

clean_hub.title: Clean slate
clean_hub.text: The system is clean, finally. SSH works, the OS is healthy. But Docker is empty: no containers, no databases, no media server. You have a clean slate and a very long list.

greg_arrives.title: Greg arrives
greg_arrives.text: Twenty minutes later Greg is at your door with two coffees, a spare SSD and a look that says 'I told you so'. He has also forgiven you for anything you said earlier.

choices.label: Let him help with the backups
Let him help you hunt the attacker
Send him home and keep going

harden.title: Harden the lab
harden.text: Key-only SSH. fail2ban. Automatic updates. You feel the smug satisfaction of locking the door after the burglar has already left, and you enjoy every second of it.

choices.label: Move the IoT junk to its own VLAN

vlan_iot.title: The IoT VLAN
vlan_iot.text: The smart fridge, the TV and the cat feeder are moved into a room with no windows and no keys. The fridge is not happy about it, but then again, it never was.

backups_clean.title: The local backups
backups_clean.text: Your NAS holds years of backups. All encrypted, with a note: 'Send 0.5 BTC for the key. You have 24 hours.' The offsite bucket was untouched, if you can unlock it.

choices.label: Search the attic for the key

attic_clean.title: The attic
attic_clean.text: Same attic, same dust, same plastic tree. A laminated card: 'OFFSITE BACKUP KEY'. You promise to buy past you a coffee.

pay_ransom_b.title: Pay the ransom
pay_ransom_b.text: The wallet is open again. You know this system is clean, which makes paying even sillier. Your finger hovers anyway.

containers_down.title: Containers offline
containers_down.text: SSH access is restored, and the base OS is healthy. However, Docker is completely empty—all your containers, databases, and media servers failed to start up automatically.

choices.label: Burn it all down and walk away

traces.title: Traces
traces.text: In /root: README_KEV.txt. 'gg ez. i was never here. - kev_the_kernel'. Next to it a hidden cron job, an unknown kernel module and a very smug piece of ASCII-art cat.

rkhunter.title: Rootkit scanner
rkhunter.text: The scanner takes forever, then prints one word in red: INFECTED. The kernel from the Reddit script carries a backdoor, and so does half of /usr/bin. Nothing on this machine can be trusted.

backups.title: The local backups
backups.text: Your NAS holds years of backups. All encrypted, with a note: 'Send 0.5 BTC for the key. You have 24 hours.' The offsite bucket is a different story, if you can unlock it.

choices.label: Search for the offsite backup key

pay_ransom.title: Pay the ransom
pay_ransom.text: The wallet is open. 0.5 BTC is more than the server cost. Your finger hovers over the button. In your head Greg says: 'Never pay.'

attic_late.title: The attic
attic_late.text: Dust, a plastic Christmas tree and a shoebox. Inside, a laminated card in your handwriting: 'OFFSITE BACKUP KEY - bucket homelab-bkp'. Past you really was a genius.

offsite_restore.title: Decrypt the offsite backup
offsite_restore.text: The key works. The bucket holds your data from last Tuesday: photos, databases, the media library. But the server in front of you is running a kernel that Kev wrote.

choices.label: Restore onto this server right now

restore_infected.title: Restore onto the infected server
restore_infected.text: Eight hours later every file is back. You sleep like a baby. At 3 a.m. your phone buzzes: everything is encrypted again. The backdoor was just waiting for fresh data.

choices.label: Throw the server out of the window

compose_git.title: Rebuild from compose files
compose_git.text: Your compose files lived in a Git repo. On this server. You stare at the empty disk and a cold realization settles in. Also, this server is still full of Kev.

choices.label: Wipe the server and start fresh

rebuild_infected.title: Rebuild on the infected host
rebuild_infected.text: The containers come up one by one. So does Kev's backdoor, now with a front-row seat to your brand-new database passwords. At dawn every service is sending spam to the entire Internet.

choices.label: Pull the plug and walk away

clean_install.title: Wipe and reinstall
clean_install.text: You boot an installer, delete every partition and watch a clean OS go on. The backdoor is gone. So is everything else, until you bring it back.

offsite_clean_restore.title: Restore the offsite backup
offsite_clean_restore.text: On a clean system the bucket finally gives up your data from last Tuesday. Photos, databases, the media library, byte by byte. It takes hours. It is the best hours of your week.

containers_up.title: Start the containers
containers_up.text: docker compose up -d. Pi-hole, Jellyfin and Vaultwarden greet you like old friends. Three containers refuse to start because their images disappeared. You decide to check the data anyway.

backup_verify.title: Checksums match
backup_verify.text: Every checksum matches. For the first time tonight something is exactly as it should be. But somewhere out there, kev_the_kernel is still laughing.

github_mirror.title: The GitHub mirror
github_mirror.text: Three months ago you mirrored the repo to GitHub 'just in case'. The compose files are there. The data is not. Rebuilding means starting every service empty.

choices.label: Rebuild every service from the mirror

survivors.title: Survivors
survivors.text: On an old laptop and the attic Raspberry Pi you find 2019 photos, a database dump from March and half the media library. It is not much, but it is yours.

rebuild_by_hand.title: Rebuild by hand
rebuild_by_hand.text: You rebuild from memory. You forget three passwords, two port numbers and why Nextcloud needed that one weird cron job. After six hours half the services work.

choices.label: Keep going until it all works
Pull the plug on this madness

rebuild_services.title: Rebuild the services
rebuild_services.text: One by one the green lights appear: Jellyfin, Nextcloud, the databases. Empty, but alive. The dashboards look beautiful and hollow, like a brand new apartment.

new_backups.title: 3-2-1 and a test
new_backups.text: Three copies. Two kinds of media. One offsite. And, for the first time in your life, an actual restore test. Past you would be proud. Future you will be grateful.

choices.label: Close the laptop. It is morning
Not done: find who did this

hunt_kev.title: Hunt for the attacker
hunt_kev.text: You have a README file, a forum name and a lot of anger. You open a terminal and a browser, and start digging.

kev_logs.title: Connection logs
kev_logs.text: He came through three proxies and a Tor exit node. Professional? Or just someone who follows tutorials very carefully?

whois_kev.title: Who is kev_the_kernel?
whois_kev.text: The username shows up on a forum, a game server and a school coding club page. His avatar is a cat in sunglasses. His latest post: 'anyone know how to bypass a firewall? asking for homework'.

choices.label: Set a honeypot to catch him

honeypot_setup.title: Set a honeypot
honeypot_setup.text: You leave a fake server with a fake SSH door 'accidentally' open, full of files named passwords_final_v2.xlsx. Now you wait.

kev_returns.title: Kev returns
kev_returns.text: At 5:12 a.m. the honeypot lights up. Someone logs in and starts exploring. He types very slowly. 'ls'. 'cd'. 'ls' again. He seems nervous.

choices.label: Open a chat window in his terminal

trace_kev.title: Trace the connection
trace_kev.text: Behind the proxies: a residential IP, then a student account at a school in the next county. Kev is, at the very most, sixteen years old.

dm_kev.title: Talk to Kev
dm_kev.text: You type: 'Hi Kev. We need to talk.' A long pause. Then: 'omg pls dont call my mom'. He sounds exactly as scared as a sixteen-year-old should.

choices.label: Tell him you are calling the police

kev_deal.title: The deal
kev_deal.text: You offer: help rebuild and harden the lab, write a full report on how he got in, and apologize to Greg. In exchange: no police, no mom. He says yes in under two seconds.

report_kev.title: Report Kev
report_kev.text: You write a thorough report: logs, timestamps, the README, the Reddit thread. The officer reads it twice, sips her coffee and says: 'Wow. Please do not hack anyone back.'

choices.label: Hand over the evidence at the station

police_station.title: At the police station
police_station.text: A detective with a tired face takes your USB stick full of logs. 'We will be in touch,' she says. 'And your data? Is it safe?'

choices.label: Tell her it is fully restored
Tell her honestly: a fifth is gone

counter_hack.title: Hack him back
counter_hack.text: You fire a stress-testing tool at his IP. It feels incredible for eleven seconds. Then you notice the IP belongs to a shared school router.

ending_full_recovery.title: Full Recovery
ending_full_recovery.text: Your lab is back, your data is back, and Kev's case sits in a folder somewhere in the county. You set up alerting, expire Greg's old key and hang a sign over the rack: 'THE RESCUE USB IS NOT DECORATION.' Pixel sleeps on the server again.

ending_phoenix.title: Phoenix
ending_phoenix.text: The photos are gone, the databases are gone. But the compose files are alive, the lab is new, and for the first time you have real backups. Starting over is the oldest homelab tradition there is.

ending_redemption.title: Redemption Arc
ending_redemption.text: Kev writes a forty-page report, fixes every hole he used, and now maintains your lab on weekends. Greg gets a public apology. The fridge lives on a VLAN. Everyone is safer, a bit embarrassed and strangely proud.

ending_justice.title: Justice, With Gaps
ending_justice.text: Kev gets a stern talk from a very tired detective. Your lab recovers, with a fifth of its memories missing. You learn to love the numbers 3-2-1, and you never forget them again.

ending_bricked.title: Bricked
ending_bricked.text: Nothing boots. Nothing mounts. Your disks hold a very organized pile of zeros. The AI would like to apologize again, but its server is not your server.

ending_paid.title: Paid and Played
ending_paid.text: The payment goes through. Nothing happens. Then a second note appears: 'Thanks! The price is now 1.0 BTC.' You are poorer, the data is still encrypted, and Kev has a new gaming PC.

ending_touch_grass.title: Touch Grass
ending_touch_grass.text: You unplug everything. The silence is wonderful. You sell the rack, buy a plant and discover that sunlight exists. You do not miss the 3 a.m. alerts. You do, slightly, miss the lab.

ending_counterhack.title: The Wrong Tool
ending_counterhack.text: You took down a school network three days before exams. Kev gets a warning. You get a very serious letter from a lawyer. Greg offers to be a character witness. It is not enough.
